# Choreography

How several moving parts stay coherent: one direction, no collisions, a set order, and a clear cause.

**Kind:** Foundation

**Storybook page:** `design-system/src/styles/MotionChoreography.mdx`

## How to read the figures

Every transition is built from three blocks (something enters, something leaves, something changes) and a short list of atoms. The rules below decide direction, space, order and cause; where there is a wrong way, it is the same scene with one rule broken, played beside the right way. Before a move plays, the screen dims and the path each part takes is drawn from start (a dot) to landing (an arrowhead). Where the lesson is order, a strip under the screen shows when each part starts. Use a figure's speed control to watch at ½× or ¼×.

## Direction

### Unify direction

When several parts move together, they move along one axis so no path crosses another and none scatters. What cannot share that axis fades in place instead of traveling. Position indicators (such as a tab indicator) track the place while the content makes its own move; step indicators change state in place.

### Move along the grid

Across, then up or down, round the corner. Never diagonal. A size change is the same: width, then height.

### Direction follows where it lives

Everything comes from where it lives and goes back there.

- A menu grows out of its trigger and shrinks back into it.
- A row grows into its page, and the page shrinks back into the row.
- A Panel and the Sidebar slide from and to their own edge.
- A section collapses up into the header that stays.
- A Flag slides in from the top-right corner along x and leaves the same way.
- On a bar anchored to the right, a control that grows (Search, the Filter count) grows to the left.
- A chevron points where the view will move.

### Back the way it came

Closing retraces the opening in reverse, one speed faster. A round trip draws one line, not two.

## Space

### Keep space

Nothing collides with a neighbor or shares its place mid-move. What leaves fades out first; only then does anything move into its space.

### Clean fades

New content begins when the old is about 90% out (`appearance.fast`, about ). A true crossfade is kept for non-text content: an image, the Blanket, or content arriving over a Skeleton.

### Stable layouts

A Skeleton holds the layout while content loads, so nothing shifts when it arrives.

### Transition every change

Every change is shown, at a volume set by how often it happens. The floor is a quiet fade, never a cut.

### Continuity

A shared container connects two views: the row becomes the record, or a quick look in a floating Panel grows into its record page. If the content is ready before the container settles, the content wins.

## Order

### Sequence and stagger

When several items arrive, they stagger 20 ms apart (or 500 ms ÷ items if shorter), so the whole set lands within half a second and reads as one arrival. The gap stays tight: the fifth row lands 80 ms after the first, while at 150 ms apart each row becomes its own event. The stagger and the clean-fade gap live in the composites, not as tokens.

### Opening a page, by moment

Stable parts arrive first, important last, top to bottom. Nothing arrives by rising; a settle of 4 px or less downward is fine, and so is a chart mark growing to its value.

- **Routine** (dozens a day): the old page fades out, the new one fades in, in place, all at once.
- **Hero** (a milestone): stable parts first, 20 ms apart, each settling 4 px or less downward. Expressive on the one Card.

### Load order

Shell and navigation, then headings and text, then data, then the primary action, then charts (which may wait until scrolled to).

### Many or one

When a few items change, each one moves (Add or remove, Reorder). When about a third or more change, swap the whole list (Swap content).

## Cause

### Same meaning, same motion

A row expanding is a reveal from its seam, and size sets the speed. A menu or a Select opening is not: it fades in place. That fade is instant from the keyboard and absent under the in-app Reduced setting; the system's reduced-motion setting keeps it. Visually similar things that live on different layers get different motion: a Panel on the page's layer pushes; one above it slides over. When one element changes both position and opacity, spatial and appearance run together.

### Forward is confirm, reverse is cancel

Cancel reverses the entrance one speed faster. Confirm fades the layer and carries the change forward: a status changes, a Flag confirms, a new record opens.

### Who started it

Input is answered at once. A system change is quieter, arrives where the system speaks (the top-right corner, a message slot above the work), and never moves what a person is touching.

### Breakpoints

A resize follows the hand: each layout change is a single jump the instant the edge crosses a breakpoint, with no animation afterward. A filter side hides at 960, quick filters fold into a menu at 768, and a rotating tablet does the same.

## Atoms

Every motion is built from these atoms, each on a family.

| Atom | Family | Where PLUS uses it |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Opacity | `appearance` | Fades everywhere; Swap content; Tooltip |
| Scale | `spatial` | Floating layers only: a Modal entering, and shrinking 2% as it leaves |
| Position | `spatial` | Panel, Sidebar, Step, indicators, Reorder |
| Mask (clip) | `spatial` | A row opening from its seam |
| Position and mask | `spatial` | A number rolling once, downward; use sparingly |
| Scale and opacity | spatial with appearance | Modal |
| Reveal from under another element | `spatial` | Breadcrumb row opening above the title |
| Position and opacity | spatial with appearance | Flag; a milestone settle |
| Corner radius, moving with size | `spatial` | Drill into and climb back out (Transitions): corners square off as the row becomes a page |
